title: Lighter Brazilian Fish Stew (Moqueca)
hook: One pot, 30 minutes: Brazilian fish stew that tastes like a beach in December
benefit: Lean protein from fish with vitamin C from peppers and lime
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb firm white fish fillets (cod, halibut or mahi mahi), cut into 2-inch pieces
1/2 cup chopped cilantro, plus more to serve
3 cups cooked brown rice, to serve
steps: Toss the fish with the juice of 1 lime, the garlic, 1/2 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Let it sit in the fridge 15 minutes while you slice the vegetables.

Heat the oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onion 4 minutes, add both bell peppers and cook 4 minutes more until soft. Stir in the paprika, cumin and red pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the coconut milk, broth and the other 1/2 teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer and cook 8 minutes so the sauce thickens a little.
Nestle the fish into the sauce in a single layer, spoon some sauce over the top, cover and simmer gently on medium-low for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 145F inside.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cilantro, scallions and the rest of the lime juice. Taste and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
Serve over brown rice with extra cilantro and lime wedges. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently so the fish stays tender.
vo_steps: Marinate the fish in lime juice, garlic, salt and pepper while you slice the vegetables.
Soften the onion and peppers in olive oil, then stir in paprika and cumin.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and broth, and simmer eight minutes.
Nestle in the fish, cover, and simmer ten minutes until it flakes.
Off the heat, stir in cilantro, scallions and lime.
